extracted.intended_audience: patent practitioners, policymakers, and interested public
extracted.subtask_description: A descriptive overview of the Unified Patent Court (UPC): its legal basis, competence, institutional structure, procedures, languages, fees, judges, and interaction with EU and national patent law. Useful for practitioners and stakeholders who need the rules and practical operation of the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence of the UPC
rubrics_metrics.description: The Unified Patent Court (UPC) has competence to hear actions regarding European patents with unitary effect and other European patents in force where normally a national court of the countries for which the agreement is applicable would have jurisdiction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of the UPC generally cover the full territory of the UPCA Contracting Member States in which the European patent has effect, but may (e.g. in actions regarding infringement) also have effect in other states where the European patent has effect. The UPC also held that it is competent for acts of patent infringement that occurred before the entry into force of the UPCA and during the period when the European patent under dispute had been opted out if eventually the opt-out has been withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of actions the UPC may hear
rubrics_metrics.description: Actions may concern inter alia patent infringement (actual patent infringement or threat of patent infringement), declarations of non-infringement, provisional and protective measures and injunctions (including preliminary injunctions), revocation (standalone revocation actions), counterclaims for revocation (by the defendant in an infringement action), and establishments of damages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The UPC competence also covers supplementary protection certificates (SPC) issued for a product protected by a European patent with or without unitary effect. The existing competences of the European Patent Office (EPO) remain unchanged: opposition procedures dealing with validity but not infringement may still be brought before the EPO during a nine-month period after grant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opt-out during transitional period
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of European patents without unitary effect, during a seven-year transitional period (which the Administrative Council may prolong by up to seven years), actions may also be brought before national courts, and proprietors of patents may opt out from the exclusive competence of the UPC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Once opted out, a European patent without unitary effect remains outside the jurisdiction of the UPC for the lifetime of the patent unless the opt-out is later withdrawn.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sources of law and applicable law (Article 24)
rubrics_metrics.description: Article 24 specifies the sources of law that the Court shall base its decisions on: European Union law (including the two EU regulations on the unitary patent), The Agreement on a Unified Patent Court (UPCA), The European Patent Convention (EPC), Other international agreements applicable to patents and binding on all member states, and National law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For the evaluation of which national law applies, regulations governing private international law (Rome I and Rome II regulations) that are part of EU law as well as multilateral agreements are leading. The UPC may request preliminary rulings from the CJEU on matters relating to EU law; such decisions are binding on the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: CJEU preliminary ruling interaction
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPC, as a court of the EU member states, may request, or in the case of the UPC Court of Appeal must request, the Court of Justice of the European Union (CJEU) to give a preliminary ruling on matters relating to European Union law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Decisions of the CJEU are then binding on the UPC. This ensures consistency with EU law despite the UPC being an international court of member states rather than an EU institution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definitions of infringement (Arts. 25–26)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 25 UPCA defines what constitutes a direct infringement of a patent under the Agreement, and Art. 26 defines what constitutes an indirect infringement thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These articles set the substantive thresholds for direct and indirect infringement under the UPCA and are the basis for infringement claims brought before the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions and permitted uses (Article 27)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement establishes several bases for the use of patented information without permission of the patent holder; exceptions in Article 27 include private and non-commercial use, breeding of patented material, use on airplanes and ships of third states while temporarily in the territory of a participating member state, and decompiling software covered by patented information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These exceptions apply to European patents both with and without unitary effect and are defenses available against infringement claims.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prior use rights (Article 28)
rubrics_metrics.description: Art. 28 UPCA provides that prior use rights (and rights derived from a prior personal possession of the patented invention) governed under the national law of a Contracting Member State may be invoked as a defense against an alleged patent infringement before the UPC but only for the Contracting Member State(s) concerned by the prior use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prior use is a national-law-based defense: the UPC applies the national law governing prior use for the territories concerned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Panel composition and judge qualifications
rubrics_metrics.description: The system includes both legally qualified and technically qualified judges, who sit in panels of three (Court of First Instance) or five (Court of Appeal) judges. Local divisions may ask (on their own or on the request of one of the parties) to have an extra technically-qualified judge added.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An overview in the article shows different mixes of legally and technically qualified judges depending on division type and case load. Panels may include judges of different nationalities. The Court of Appeal may include panels that must request CJEU preliminary rulings for EU law matters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Language of proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Proceedings before a local or regional division generally take place in the local language, in an official language of the EPO (English, German or French) if the division has designated such a language, or in the language in which the patent was granted if the parties and the panel all agree. Before the central division, proceedings take place in the language in which the patent was granted (English, German or French). The Court of Appeal generally proceeds in the language used before the Court of First Instance, or in the language in which the patent was granted if the parties all agree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judge-rapporteur may decide to use a national language for oral proceedings and/or the decision. Local divisions' language choices are listed by country; central divisions use EPO languages.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proceedings structure (written, interim, oral)
rubrics_metrics.description: The proceedings before the Court comprise three consecutive parts: a written procedure, an interim procedure, and an oral procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This tripartite structure frames how cases are managed from filing through interim measures to oral hearings; procedural rules (timelines, filings) are set out in the UPC Rules of Procedure referenced in the article.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeal procedure and time limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Appeals against decisions of the Court of First Instance may be brought before the Court of Appeal within two months of the date of the notification of the decision. Appeals against certain orders (such as an order to produce evidence) may be brought within 15 calendar days of notification. Appeals may be brought on both points of law and questions of facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Court of Appeal may refer cases of exceptional importance to the full Court to ensure unity and consistency of UPC case law.

rubrics_metrics.name: Court fees and value-based fee structure
rubrics_metrics.description: To finance its budget, the UPC's financial revenues include court fees which the Administrative Committee adopts and periodically reviews. Some court fees are fixed fees, whereas others are constituted of a combination of a fixed fee and an additional value-based fee, i.e. a fee depending on the value of the action (the 'value in dispute').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrative Committee sets fees; value-based fees scale with the value of the proceedings. Fee schedules are published by the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recoverable costs and caps
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPCA provides that the unsuccessful party in UPC proceedings shall bear 'reasonable and proportionate legal costs and other expenses incurred by the successful party'. The recoverable costs are capped, and the applicable ceilings depend on the value of the action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This loser-pays principle is tempered by statutory caps (ceilings) that vary by value band; exact ceilings and calculation methods are set out in the UPCA and implementing provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence over Supplementary Protection Certificates (SPCs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPC competence also covers supplementary protection certificates (SPC) issued for a product protected by a European patent with or without unitary effect.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SPC-related disputes that concern a product protected by a European patent may be litigated before the UPC under the UPCA competence rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interaction with EPO opposition and limits of EPO competence
rubrics_metrics.description: An opposition procedure dealing with the validity of the patent but not with infringement may still be brought before the EPO during a nine-month period after the grant of the patent. Decisions by the EPO are valid throughout the territory in which the European patent is valid.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opposition at the EPO is centralised for validity issues; UPC handles infringement and revocation actions as set out in the UPCA, and both systems can interact (e.g. parallel litigation consequences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Local and regional divisions: establishment and territorial jurisdiction
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting states are free to set up local or regional divisions up to a maximum number depending on case load. The characteristics of the divisions and their territorial jurisdiction are set out (Annex II of the UPCA).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Of the countries that ratified, some are not part of a local or regional division; actions that could normally be brought before those countries' local divisions can be brought before the Central division. Distribution of cases within the central division is set out in Annex II.

rubrics_metrics.name: Central division thematic sections and locations
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court of First Instance has a central division with its seat in Paris, and thematic sections in Munich (mechanical engineering cases) and Milan. The distribution of cases within the central division is set out in Annex II of the UPCA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A change to the UPC Agreement entered into force on 1 July 2024 to accommodate replacement of London with Milan as a thematic section, with case-load repartition among Munich and Paris.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation rules and the European Patent Litigation Certificate (EPLC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Rules regarding representation before the court include the requirements for the European Patent Litigation Certificate (for which academic courses will be accredited) as well as equivalent certificates that are accepted during a transition period. Patent attorneys with a law degree are exempted from the EPLC.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisional representation rules were approved during preparatory stages; accredited courses and transitional equivalences are provided for. Representation requirements affect who may plead before the UPC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative and advisory governance structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Three committees ensure the effective implementation and operation of the Agreement: an Administrative Committee (one representative of each Contracting Member State), a Budget Committee (one representative of each Contracting Member State), and an Advisory Committee comprising patent judges and practitioners tasked among others with advising on selection of judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Administrative Committee adopts fees and Rules; the Advisory Committee advises on judge selection; preparatory and select committees (e.g., EPO Select Committee) performed implementation work before entry into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Provisional application provisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Provisional application of the UPC Agreement was triggered to enable preparation for the proper functioning of the court. Provisional application allows the hiring of judges and moving to the court premises.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provisional application started on 19 January 2022 after required states ratified or indicated completion of parliamentary processes; it permits preparatory administrative and operational steps before full entry into force.

rubrics_metrics.name: Conditions for entry into force of the UPCA
rubrics_metrics.description: The Agreement entered into force after meeting three predefined conditions on 1 June 2023: amendment of the Brussels I Regulation, ratification by the three largest patent-granting EU member states (France, Germany, Italy) in 2012, and ratification or accession by at least thirteen states in total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For signatories ratifying or acceding after entry into force, their membership takes effect on the first day of the fourth month after deposit of instrument of ratification or accession.

rubrics_metrics.name: Referral to full Court for unity and consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: The Court of Appeal may refer cases of exceptional importance to the full Court (the Court of Appeal sitting as a full Court), in order to ensure 'unity and consistency of the case law of the Court'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This mechanism is used to maintain coherent jurisprudence across the UPC's multi-jurisdictional remit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Competence for infringement before and during opt-out periods
rubrics_metrics.description: The UPC has held that it is competent for acts of patent infringement that occurred before the entry into force of the UPCA and during the period when the European patent under dispute had been opted out if eventually the opt-out has been withdrawn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This establishes that temporal aspects (pre-entry or during opt-out) do not necessarily preclude UPC jurisdiction if opt-out status changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judicial training and mediation/arbitration centres
rubrics_metrics.description: Training of judges takes place in Budapest, and Lisbon and Ljubljana host seats of a patent mediation and arbitration centre. A training centre for judges and candidate judges was opened (Budapest, 13 March 2014).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The presence of training and mediation centres supports judge qualification standards and alternative dispute resolution options within the UPC framework.
